methodologyCaveat: The 'notIndexed' group (n=1017) is a REAL, live-GSC-confirmed sample built from the two not-indexed reason buckets captured this session (see fresh-gsc-snapshot.json) -- every URL in it is a genuine live confirmation. The 'rest' group (n=331) is NOT a clean 'confirmed indexed' set: it is simply every comparison page NOT captured in either not-indexed sample, and both bucket samples were partial (fresh-gsc-snapshot.json's toolLimitation note), so 'rest' is contaminated with an unknown number of additional not-indexed pages this session's sampling missed. Because of this contamination, the dimensions below should be read as INSUFFICIENT SAMPLE for a fully clean causal comparison, not as definitive proof of no effect -- but the contamination only works AGAINST finding a real difference (it dilutes 'rest' toward looking more like 'notIndexed'), so a genuinely large true effect would likely still show through partially. None of these numbers show that.

dimensions.note: Directly consistent with the master mission's own standing grounding rule ('never assume more internal links is the answer' -- the Pipedrive lesson). This is fresh, page-level evidence for comparisons specifically: internal link count does not separate indexed from not-indexed comparison pages. Do not launch a link-building campaign for comparison pages on this basis.

Both groups sit at depth 2 (behind a category or software page) as their typical case; max depth sitewide for comparisons is 3, with 0 unreachable pages. Click depth is not a plausible bottleneck for comparison indexation given how shallow the whole site already is.
A ~2.5 point gap on a noisy, contaminated control group is not meaningful.

dimensions.dimension: average constituent factual-depth score (mean of both products' software-page scores)
dimensions.verdict: NO_OBSERVED_DIFFERENCE (if anything, slightly the other direction)
dimensions.note: This is the most important result in this file. The not-indexed group's average constituent factual depth is NOT lower than the comparison group -- it is marginally higher. This measurement predates this session's own Wave-3-style comparison work (which targets specific low-depth products), so it is not evidence that such work is pointless, but it IS evidence that factual depth alone does not explain most of the sitewide comparison non-indexation problem. Per Part 5's own framing: 'If factual depth no longer separates the groups... that is important.' Recommendation: continue enriching specific low-depth products for their own sake (real product-page quality, compounding value for /software/ pages and alternative-guides) but do not expect that alone to be the dominant lever for comparison-page indexation at scale.

dimensions.dimension: minimum constituent factual-depth score (the weaker of the two sides)
dimensions.note: Same direction as the average -- the weaker side of a not-indexed pair is not systematically weaker than the weaker side of the comparison group.

categoryLevelCaveat: This null result is specific to the individual comparison-page level. The separate category-indexation-map.json DOES show categories with fewer avg inbound links tend to have a higher never-crawled-discovered rate -- but that is a category-level, not page-level, correlation, and is very plausibly confounded by category size/maturity rather than a direct per-page causal link. Do not use the category-level pattern to justify a per-page link-building intervention; the page-level comparator above argues directly against that.
overallConclusion: Neither internal-link authority, click depth, nor factual depth cleanly separates indexed from not-indexed comparison pages at the individual-page level in this (partially contaminated) sample. This is a genuine, evidence-backed reason to be cautious about over-investing in any single mechanical lever for the comparison-page indexation problem at scale, and argues for the more surgical, evidence-selected approach this session actually took (enrich specific low-depth products with real demand behind them; do not attempt a blanket link or content campaign across all 1348 comparisons).
